problem: Post-selection tests for estimated spatial domain boundaries under a latent-field continuity null (count splitting + boundary-discontinuity statistic)
source: ClusterDE (PMC10401959; Discussion): its synthetic null assumes a single homogeneous domain and the authors list gaining power while holding FDR as future work. Data fission/thinning limitations paper (arXiv:2405.13591, Discussion): thinning assumes a homogeneous distribution, i.e. no true clusters, so mixture structure is needed. MM-test (arXiv:2603.09061, Discussion): cluster-then-test gives invalid p-values (double dipping). Paraphrase of the shared gap: no valid p-value for 'is this estimated spatial domain boundary real' when spatial dependence is present and true domains exist.
formulation: Y_i ~ Poisson(s_i * lambda(x_i)) with latent random field lambda (Matern, unknown range) and depth s_i. Thin Y into Y1=Bin(Y,eps), Y2=Y-Y1, independent given (lambda,s) even though lambda is spatially dependent. Estimate a boundary Gamma-hat from Y1 with any spatially smoothed clusterer. Test on Y2 the continuity null H0: lambda has no jump across Gamma-hat, using a local-linear boundary-discontinuity statistic with bandwidth h. The naive between-domain mean test is NOT valid even with perfectly independent folds, because under a continuous random field domains differ in mean; the null must be continuity, not equal means.
closest_prior: Queries (arXiv, Crossref, web; see mine_STSTAT_queries.csv, 10 on this problem): count splitting spatial, data thinning random field, post-clustering inference spatial, RD with estimated cutoff, geographic RD unknown boundary, SI change point. Closest: Neufeld et al. count splitting (arXiv:2207.00554; NB version arXiv:2307.12985), Dharamshi et al. generalized thinning (arXiv:2303.12931), SI for clustering pipelines (arXiv:2603.18413), SI for change points (arXiv:1706.00514, 2104.12022, 2110.08989), Bayesian RD with unknown cutoff (10.1214/25-ba1575), rd2d and SpatialRDD (CRAN), spatial RDD under spillovers (10.2139/ssrn.7266687), wombling, ClusterDE. I found no paper that combines thinning of a latent-field count process with boundary-discontinuity inference at a data-selected spatial boundary. Caveats: arXiv phrase search is weak for this topic, Semantic Scholar was rate-limited so not used, and a SpatialLens query on count splitting for spatial DE in the digest (section C) returned nothing but was ungraded. Each component is published; only the combination and the gradient-selection inflation result are unseen.

problem: Identification and valid tests of neighbour (context) effects under transcript spillover, calibrated with negative-control genes
source: Nature Genetics segmentation-error paper (10.1038/s41588-025-02497-4; Discussion): residual admixture remains after correction, and a sufficiently powered downstream test will rediscover it, so downstream methods should explicitly control for segmentation errors. smiDE (10.1186/s13059-025-03867-1; Discussion): heuristic covariate adjustment/gene filtering for misassignment, spatial confounding unresolved. MisTIC (PMC12724677; Discussion): effectiveness depends on initial boundary quality and gives no per-cell confidence. Spacelink (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.24.678397; Limitations 7): single-cell platform results depend on segmentation quality.
formulation: Observed y_i^g = (1-a_i) x_i^g + a_i * sum_j w(d_ij) x_j^g + noise, x = true own-cell expression, w a distance-decay spillover kernel. Estimand: theta_g = effect of neighbour cell-type composition on the focal cell's own expression of gene g. Naive regression targets theta_g + a * (cross-type expression contrast), a bias that does not vanish with n. Negative-control genes (zero true expression in the focal type, e.g. mutually exclusive markers) identify a(d). Questions: sharp partial-identification set for theta_g without controls, point identification and asymptotic normality with controls and estimated a(d), and false-positive rate of the naive test as a function of leakage fraction.
closest_prior: Queries (12 logged): transcript misassignment/negative control/spillover in ST (web, arXiv, Crossref), ambient RNA decontamination, spatial moving-average outcome error, peer-effects measurement error. ST side found only correction methods: Mitchel et al. NMF+CRF, Ergen & Yosef probabilistic diffusion, Wu/Beechem/Danaher CosMx reassignment (all as described in the Nat Methods Xenium paper 10.1038/s41592-026-03089-8, excerpts only), MisTIC, smiDE; also ambient-RNA decontamination benchmark 10.64898/2026.01.13.699237 (title only). Econometrics side: measurement error and peer effects in networks (arXiv:2608.00336; noisy proxies can inflate peer effects, identification via network structure), SAR with covariate measurement error (arXiv:2402.04593), spatially correlated measurement error (10.21203/rs.3.rs-9706755/v1; abstract not read). Those treat covariate error, not outcome contamination by neighbours' latent outcomes with exclusion genes. Risk: a referee may see this as proximal/negative-control reasoning applied to a spatial moving-average outcome, so the theory contribution could be judged incremental.

problem: Valid cell-type-specific spatial tests when composition is a deconvolution estimate: generated simplex regressors with spatially correlated error
source: Celina (Nat Commun 10.1038/s41467-025-56280-4; Discussion, limitation 1): accuracy depends on deconvolution accuracy, power ordering true > CARD > RCTD; also reports CSIDE p-values inflated (genomic inflation 1.23-4.12). Spacelink (limitation 5): cell-type version relies on spot-level proportions, errors from poorly matched references propagate into inference. FlashDeconv (PMC12776147; Limitations): reference incompleteness biases estimates.
formulation: y_s ~ NB(mu_s), log mu_s = sum_k pi_sk beta_gk + f_g(x_s), but only pi-hat_s = pi_s + e_s is available, e_s on the simplex, spatially smooth, covariance depending on pi_s and reference mismatch. Test beta_gk = c or a cell-type-specific spatial variance component. Question: size distortion of Wald/score tests that plug in pi-hat, in particular spurious spatial variance attributed to type k because e_s is itself spatially structured.
closest_prior: Queries (9 logged): generated regressors/cell-type proportions (arXiv), errors-in-variables deconvolution, estimated proportions downstream tests, Murphy-Topel two-step, ct-SVG error propagation, compositional covariates with measurement error. Closest: generated-regressor inference in econometrics (10.2139/ssrn.7493339; 10.2139/ssrn.7153809), inference on proportions estimated from bulk data (JASA 10.1080/01621459.2024.2382435, no abstract retrieved), a bulk measurement-error-adjusted deconvolution framework seen only as a ResearchGate snippet, ctSVG (10.21203/rs.3.rs-5655066/v1) and STANCE (10.1101/2024.09.22.614385), both of which plug in estimated composition. I found no treatment of spatially structured simplex error for ST tests. Risk: the non-spatial core is classical generated-regressor theory, so novelty rests on the spatial error structure and the simplex constraint.

problem: Spatially variable gene tests with a spatially structured, partially observed depth/composition nuisance: estimand, null and robust calibration
source: SVG benchmark (Genome Biol 10.1186/s13059-025-03731-2; Discussion): most methods give poorly calibrated p-values; authors advise rank thresholds instead of significance. Multi-scale testing (PMC13015534; limitations): moment matching cannot capture tail behaviour of zero-inflated quadratic forms, saddlepoint approximation could tighten calibration. Spacelink (limitation 2): residual capture-efficiency differences across platforms. smiDE: spatial confounding with structured covariates.
formulation: Y_ig ~ Poisson(s(x_i) * lambda_g(x_i)), depth field s latent and smooth, proxied by library size L_i = sum_g Y_ig, which contains signal. H0_g: lambda_g constant. Normalising by L_i can induce spatial structure in null genes when many programmes vary spatially (compositional effect). Estimate s from negative-control genes; study tests conditional on s-hat. Target: size distortion as a function of the spatial-frequency error of s-hat, and a Monte Carlo (field-fitted) null that is robust to it.
closest_prior: Queries (7 logged, Crossref/arXiv, mostly weak): CRT/permutation under spatial confounding, library size as confounder in SVG, restricted randomisation for autocorrelated fields, robust CRT under misspecification. Closest: SVG benchmark, SOAAR (10.64898/2026.07.06.736800, abstract only: autocorrelation-preserving resampling for gene-gene correlation tests), a title raising the library-size question empirically (10.1101/2025.09.15.676443, 'Library Size in Spatial ATAC-seq: Technical Confounder or Biology?', abstract not read), multi-scale test. The topic is poorly covered by arXiv/Crossref, so a missed prior is plausible, especially in the geostatistics literature on testing correlation between autocorrelated fields and in the spoon-type SVG normalisation papers (not retrieved).

problem: Scale decomposition identity for image-predicted expression: what Moran's I and per-gene PCC of predictions can certify
source: Histology-prediction benchmark (PMC13445978; Methods/Discussion): introduces a Moran-inspired spatial metric, reports PCC only 0.1-0.3. Active-spot benchmark (arXiv:2609.27208; Discussion and Future Work): PCC/ARI reversal not reproduced on a second cohort, comparisons descriptive, pointwise and spatial measures should be reported separately. A published prediction paper reports Moran's I of its predictions as evidence of validity (FOCST, PLOS Comput Biol 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014762, search excerpt).
formulation: For a predictor yhat = f(image features) on a spatial graph, decompose PCC and Moran's I over graph-Fourier scales; relate I(yhat) to I(y) and to residual spatial autocorrelation; give conditions under which I(yhat) exceeds I(y) (smoother predictor) and when scale-resolved correlation is identified from within-donor data.
closest_prior: Queries (5 logged). Closest and decisive: Octave (10.64898/2026.09.25.754484, Oct 2026, abstract only) states PCC does not distinguish spatial scales and builds a domain oracle and scale-resolved evaluation; kriging smoothing-effect literature is classical (queries did not retrieve it, so I cite none). The digest also lists related excluded ideas (SCALE, signature plot, gene-gene correlation inflation in predictions). Remainder is theory for Moran's I of predictions and donor-level intervals, which looks thin.

problem: Spatial confounding in cell-type or domain differential expression when the covariate is a spatially structured label
source: smiDE (10.1186/s13059-025-03867-1; Discussion): spatial confounding when the covariate has strong spatial structure (niches, regions) is a key limitation; joint multi-sample spatial modelling is the next step.
formulation: y_s = x_s' beta + w(s) + e with x_s a label (cell type or domain) correlated with the Gaussian random field w; question: what GLS/restricted-spatial-regression estimators target when the label was itself derived from expression, and the identifiable beta under smoothness mismatch.
